claims.text: An alternative framework classifies nudges into two categories: Type 1 and Type 2.
The evidence base for the effectiveness of nudges in the health domain is limited due to empirical issues of internal and external reliability.

evidence.description: The authors 'propose an alternative framework that helps to classify nudges into two types (Type 1 and Type 2).'
Evaluation of nudge research in health draws 'attention to critical empirical issues (internal and external reliability) that explain the limited evidence base for their effectiveness.'

methodologies.name: Type 1 and Type 2 nudge taxonomy
methodologies.description: A theoretical classification framework categorizing behavioral nudges into Type 1 and Type 2.

limitations.text: The conventional theoretical framework that nudges are based on presents conceptual problems.
Existing empirical studies of nudges in the health domain exhibit limited internal and external reliability.
